entries.name: mcp__github__issue_read
entries.description: Get information about a specific issue in a GitHub repository.

method.description:
The read operation to perform on a single issue.
Options are:
1. get - Get issue details. Also returns best-effort hierarchy flags (`has_parent`, `has_children`); `parent` and `sub_issues_summary` are optional relationship summaries, and `closed_by_pull_requests` summarizes the pull requests configured to close the issue as `total_count` plus up to 5 `references`.
2. get_comments - Get issue comments.
3. get_sub_issues - Get sub-issues (children) of the issue.
4. get_parent - Get the parent issue, if this issue is a sub-issue of another.
5. get_labels - Get labels assigned to the issue.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

entries.name: mcp__github__list_pull_requests
entries.description: List pull requests in a GitHub repository. If the user specifies an author, then DO NOT use this tool and use the search_pull_requests tool instead.

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each pull request. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

head.description: Filter by head user/org and branch

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

entries.name: mcp__github__search_issues
entries.description: Search issues using natural-language semantic matching. Best for conceptual or paraphrased queries (e.g. "login fails after password reset"). Already scoped to is:issue.

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each issue result. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body', 'reactions', and 'labels' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

owner.description: Optional repository owner. If provided with repo, only issues for this repository are listed.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

query.description: The search query, as natural language. When the user gives alternative wordings, include them as plain words rather than joining them with OR.

repo.description: Optional repository name. If provided with owner, only issues for this repository are listed.

sort.description: Sort field by number of matches of categories, defaults to best match

{"number":1869,"title":"Reorganize claudinite-tasks: roles as folders, the simulator as the harness, principles as the spec","body":"Tracking issue. The plan below is approved by the owner (2026-09-07) and is append-only from here; links comment their results underneath.

## The problem

`packs/claudinite-tasks/` is the old flat `engine/scheduler/` copied in whole (#1326): 32 modules at the root, a `queue/` that is both workflow ABI and most of the logic, GitHub calls at 29 REST paths spread over a dozen modules, and 9,500 lines of design prose whose only executable counterpart is a simulator that re-implements the mechanism beside the code it describes. Nothing says which part owns what, a claim in the docs can be false without anything going red, and the scenario suite proves the model rather than the engine. (#1478 carries the layout analysis, validated 2026-09-07 in its comments; #1347 the simulator analysis.)

## End state

- **Roles are folders, and the graph between them is enforced.** `src/contract/` (what a task declares), `src/items/` (the work item as data), `src/world/` (the only modules that reach outside: GitHub, sessions, Actions, git, subprocesses, the clock — each a typed port with named operations; the real implementation alone knows REST paths and env names), `src/signals/`, and the stages `src/schedule/`, `src/execute/`, `src/session/`, `src/deliver/`, `src/recover/`, `src/adopt/`. `contract/` and `items/` import no stage; `world/` imports nothing above it; stages form a DAG. The `barriers` pack's config carries the import rules; a declared line-match check keeps `fetch(`, `process.env`, `child_process` and `new Date()` out of everything but `world/`.
- **The frozen surfaces have runnable shims, each annotated with its retirement.** `queue/` holds the six workflow entry points (`scheduler-run`, `drain-dispatch`, `workflow-failure`, `executor`, `executor-continuation`, `tick`), `instructions.md`, and `tasks/implement-request/` (the worker path every adopted issue's machine block names) — entry shims, never logic. `executor.md` stays where routines point. `shared-code/*` re-exports `src/contract/` and retires on a stated convergence window.
- **The simulator runs the real code and fakes only the world.** `test/sim/world/{clock,github,actions,sessions,agents,humans}.mjs` implement the same ports as `src/world/`, in memory, with GitHub's limitations (rate limits, non-atomic label swaps, stale lists, 1-second comment timestamps with strictly increasing ids, dropped events, 422 on unknown labels) and the platform's (late and dropped cron fires, start latency, the concurrency group, job kills at the timeout, billed minutes) as switchable faults. Agentic work is scripted: a fired session runs the real session-side code against the fake GitHub and does what its script says (leaves a PR, prints its record, takes N virtual minutes, dies, refuses). `sim.mjs` keeps no model of the mechanism.
- **The docs are one principles file, every claim executable.** `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` states the mechanism as *Y happens when Z* claims, each citing the scenario test that proves it; a guard fails when a claim cites no existing scenario or a scenario is cited by no claim. The four `DESIGN.md`s, `SCENARIOS.md`, `RESEARCH.md` and the audit are deleted; what still holds lives in module headers, the pack README, and the principles.
- **The code is rewritten under frozen contracts and frozen tests.** After the roles split, each stage is reimplemented for simplicity inside its own folder, with no change under `test/` and no change to any contract: the `world/` ports, the `shared-code/` exports, the wire vocabulary (titles, labels, status and outcome words, body blocks, run-record lines, the machine block), task names, the workflow ABI. Contract-pinning tests are written before the first rewrite. Unit tests pin the module paths and exports they import, so a rewrite simplifies inside those and may delete a module only when no test imports it.
- **The machinery measures itself.** A `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json` of its own, independent of the session-usage fold: per workflow per day the runs, the billed minutes (job durations from the jobs listing, rounded per job as GitHub bills; verified against the docs at link time) and the spend they imply at a configured rate (zero on a public repo); per run the API calls and wall time per phase, from a `claudinite-run-cost` record each run prints; per task the outcomes, parks by kind, and latency samples tick→item, item→pick, pick→hand-off, hand-off→converge. The dashboard renders reliability (success rate window over window, parks, latency quantiles) and cost (minutes, spend, calls) per task and per member.

Alternatives considered: keeping `gh(path)` as the seam and faking REST (the fake becomes a GitHub emulator that every new call site silently widens); keeping the sim as an independent model (it can never say whether the engine does what the design says); trimming the design docs instead of deleting them (a trimmed narrative still describes a past state nothing verifies).

## Standing conditions (owner, 2026-09-07)

Two risks this plan exists to catch: over-complexity with no clear separation of concerns, and a failure that blocks task execution on every member. The conditions, each carried by a mechanism rather than a reminder:

1. **Rewrites change no tests.** Every rewrite link's policy is `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/<stage>`; a file under `test/` parks the PR.
2. **Folder separation is strict.** The barrier rules and the line-match check land with S1; a rewrite whose diff leaves its folder parks.
3. **Contracts do not change** — labels, status and outcome words, task names, field names, the machine block, run-record lines, the `shared-code/` exports, the workflow ABI paths, the `world/` port names. R0 pins them; a rewrite cannot edit the pins (condition 1), so a contract change parks.
4. **No new design vocabulary without approval.** This plan approves exactly: the folder names above, `test/sim/world/`, `docs/PRINCIPLES.md`, `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json`, `claudinite-run-cost`. Any other new label, word, field, file-name convention or term is filed as a question, never introduced.
5. **Breaking changes get hand-holding.** A change to what a member's mount, workflow or routine does — a path, a label, a field, a file a member reads — parks as `needs-human-action` naming the change; the folders `queue/`, `shared-code/`, `stubs/`, `worldRules/`, `workRules/`, `migrations/` sit outside every automerge policy in this plan.
6. **Subagents are fine inside a link**; a link stays one PR with one exit.

## Work paths

| Path | Scope (touches) | Contract (must not change) | Exit (readable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P — Principles** | `docs/`, the `test/sim/` guard, `§` pointers in code comments and pack prose, the README pointer | scenario test titles (the claim map binds to them) | `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` is the only file under `docs/`, the guard is green both ways |
| **S — Structure** | the whole pack tree, consumer packs' import lines, the barrier config, the pack README | the wire vocabulary, the seven frozen paths, every `shared-code/` export, `executor.md`/`instructions.md` locations | suite green, the barrier and line-match checks green on the new tree, this repo's own scheduler and executor green from the shim paths |
| **H — Harness** | `test/sim/` only; an engine fix a scenario proves necessary parks | scenario titles; every contract | `sim.mjs` holds no mechanism model; every scenario drives the real modules through the fake world |
| **R — Rewrite** | one `src/<stage>/` per link | everything above, `test/` untouched | the stage's line and module counts down, suite and sim green |
| **M — Measure** | `tasks/`, `src/world/` (the counter), the dashboard's readers and one panel | the session-usage file's keys during the stated window | the tasks usage file lands nightly and the dashboard reads it |
| **V — Verify** | nothing in the tree | — | runs read green; the retrospective answered against numbers recorded before and after R |

## Phase 0 — out-of-band setup

None. Every read uses the Action's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

## The plan

Each step is a queued link (`task:origin:ad-hoc`, `Blocked-by:` its predecessor). The chain advances on a link's exit reading true, never on its run having happened; every link's brief opens by reading its predecessor's artifact on `main` and converges as `action` naming the unmerged link when it is absent. No link's PR carries `Closes #<this issue>`.

- [ ] **P** — `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` from the current docs and the coverage map, the two-way claim guard, the design docs deleted, every `§` pointer re-pointed at a principle or dropped. *Policy: nothing (the principles are the design).*
- [ ] **S1** (#1478) — the re-shelve: `src/<role>/`, typed world ports with injectable shells, `pickOrder`/`evaluatePrecondition` extracted, the seven frozen paths as runnable shims carrying `@legacy-tolerance … retire:#S2`, `shared-code/` re-exporting `src/contract/`, consumer imports rewritten, tests mirroring `src/`, the barrier rules and line-match check, the README's layout table, `run.mjs`/`slots.mjs` and the slot-era `dispatch`/`resolve-dispatch`/`validate-dispatch` retired or placed per fielded history. *Policy: nothing (wide by nature).*
- [ ] **H1** (#1347) — the fake world in `test/sim/world/`, promoted from `executor-loop.test.mjs`'s fake repo; the loop test moved onto it with no behaviour change. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test`.*
- [ ] **H2** — every scenario ported onto the real code, the model deleted slice by slice, the "unsimulated world" table becoming each fake module's header plus limitation scenarios with their principles. A disagreement is decided by the principle; an engine fix parks. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/docs`.*
- [ ] **M1** — the tasks usage file: a `tasks-usage-fold` task, the run-cost record printed by each run and counted at the world ports, billed minutes from the jobs listing, the session fold dropping task keys after a stated window, the dashboard reading the new file. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/world; under:packs/claudinite-dashboard` (an engine `.gitattributes` seed parks).*
- [ ] **M2** — the dashboard's reliability and cost panel, per task and per member, window over window. *Policy: nothing (first render).*
- [ ] **R0** — the contract pins. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test`.*
- [ ] **R1** — rewrite `contract/` + `items/`. *Policy: `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/contract; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/src/items`.*
- [ ] **R2** — rewrite `schedule/` + `signals/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **R3** — rewrite `execute/`. *Policy: its folder.*
- [ ] **R4** — rewrite `session/` + `deliver/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **R5** — rewrite `recover/` + `adopt/` + the pack's own `tasks/`. *Policy: its folders.*
- [ ] **S2** — retire the `shared-code/` shims and the barrier's second allow path, 14 days after S1 merged (the window an active member needs to receive the engine that unblocks a held-back pack; a member stale longer takes the break). *Policy: nothing.*
- [ ] **V1** — after S1 merged, this repo's next scheduler run and executor run are green from the shim paths. No PR.
- [ ] **V2** — the retrospective, 7 days after the last of R5, M2, S2. No PR.

### The graph

```
P → S1 → H1 → H2 → R0 → R1 → R2 → R3 → R4 → R5 ─┐
     ├→ M1 → M2 ─────────────────────────────────┼→ V2
     ├→ S2 (Not-before: S1 + 14d) ───────────────┘
     └→ V1
```

M runs beside the main chain so the numbers exist before R starts.

### Human gates

`nothing` links: P, S1, M2, S2 — four. Expected parks: H2 (an engine fix beside the port), M1 (a seed outside its folders). **About six arrivals of the owner's attention across fifteen links.**

## Not in this chain

- #1346 (the `taskScheduler` config move) stays behind #1317; S1 leaves the config reader where it is.
- #1816 (the pack-boundary retrospective) stays under #1317; V2 is this plan's own.
- #1328 (the `updates/*` shims) is #1317's last code link.
- Simplifying the unit-test tree itself (re-homing tests onto stage entry points) — a later plan, once R shows which module paths the tests still need.

## The retrospective's brief (V2, written now)

Expected after the chain, against the numbers M1 records before R0:

| Measure | Now | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| non-test modules in the pack | 90 | ≤ 60 |
| non-test lines | ~11,000 | ≤ 7,000 |
| design-doc lines under `docs/` | 9,483 | ≤ 400 |
| scenarios | 82 | ≥ 100; the sim suite ≤ 5 s |
| principles without a scenario | not measured | 0 (the guard) |
| API calls per scheduler tick on a quiet day | not measured | recorded before R, not higher after |
| billed minutes per member-day | not measured | recorded before R, not higher after |
| barrier firings on a stage edge | none possible | 0 after S1 |
| `shared-code/` importers | 40 files | 0 after S2 |

Signals — misuse: a barrier finding on a stage edge, or a waiver added to let one through. Overuse: a shim still imported after S2. Underuse: a scenario cited by no principle; a panel nobody opened (page hits are not recorded — say so). The decision to re-examine: whether the roles are the right cut, read off which folders each of R1–R5's diffs actually touched and which parks they took.

## Corrections made while filing (2026-09-07, before any implementation)

- **S2 is dropped.** `shared-code/` stays the published surface, unrenamed: it publishes delivery and GitHub helpers too, which `contract/` would misname, and keeping the address needs no tolerance and nothing to retire. Its modules re-export from the new internal homes (S1's brief). The `nothing` gates are therefore three: P, S1, M2. The `shared-code/` importers row in the retrospective's table reads *unchanged by design* instead of *0 after S2*.
- **M1 keeps the session fold's task keys.** Their writers are marked `@deprecated` naming the tasks file as successor; removal is a later plan rather than a windowed tolerance inside this one.
- **V1 re-arms itself** (`Not-before:` to now + `Retry-every:`, status cleared) while the next tick has not come, rather than parking on a person.
- **The two reused issues are not sub-issues** of this one: the API needs their database id, which the session's tools do not return. They are linked here instead.

## Where each link stands

| Link | Issue | Waits on | Policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | #1870 | — | nothing |
| S1 | #1478 | #1870 | nothing |
| H1 | #1347 | #1478 | `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test` |
| H2 | #1871 | #1347 | `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test; under:packs/claudinite-tasks/docs` |
| M1 | #1872 | #1478 | `under:…/tasks; under:…/src/world; under:…/src/items; under:packs/claudinite-dashboard` |
| M2 | #1874 | #1872 | nothing |
| V1 | #1873 | #1478 | no PR |
| R0 | #1875 | #1871 | `under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test` |

| R2 | #1877 | #1876 | `under:…/src/schedule; under:…/src/signals` |
| R3 | #1878 | #1877 | `under:…/src/execute` |
| R4 | #1879 | #1878 | `under:…/src/session; under:…/src/deliver` |
| R5 | #1880 | #1879 | `under:…/src/recover; under:…/src/adopt; under:…/tasks` |
| V2 | #1881 | #1880, #1874 + 7 days | no PR |

4. **No new design vocabulary without approval.** This plan approves exactly: the folder names above, `test/sim/world/`, `docs/PRINCIPLES.md`, `tasks-usage.GENERATED.json`, `claudinite-run-cost`. Any other new label, word, field, file-name convention or term is filed as a question, never introduced.
5. **Breaking changes get hand-holding.** A change to what a member's mount, workflow or routine does — a path, a label, a field, a file a member reads — parks as `needs-human-action` naming the change; the folders `queue/`, `shared-code/`, `stubs/`, `worldRules/`, `workRules/`, `migrations/` sit outside every automerge policy in this plan.
6. **Subagents are fine inside a link**; a link stays one PR with one exit.

| Path | Scope (touches) | Contract (must not change) | Exit (readable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P — Principles** | `docs/`, the `test/sim/` guard, `§` pointers in code comments and pack prose, the README pointer | scenario test titles (the claim map binds to them) | `docs/PRINCIPLES.md` is the only file under `docs/`, the guard is green both ways |

Each step is a queued link (`task:origin:ad-hoc`, `Blocked-by:` its predecessor). The chain advances on a link's exit reading true, never on its run having happened; every link's brief opens by reading its predecessor's artifact on `main` and converges as `action` naming the unmerged link when it is absent. - [ ] **S1** (#1478) — the re-shelve: `src/<role>/`, typed world ports with injectable shells, `pickOrder`/`evaluatePrecondition` extracted, the seven frozen paths as runnable shims carrying `@legacy-tolerance … retire:#S2`, `shared-code/` re-exporting `src/contract/`, consumer imports rewritten, tests mirroring `src/`, the barrier rules and line-match check, the README's layout table, `run.mjs`/`slots.mjs` and the slot-era `dispatch`/`resolve-dispatch`/`validate-dispatch` retired or placed per fielded history. *Policy: nothing (wide by nature).*

`nothing` links: P, S1, M2, S2 — four. Expected parks: H2 (an engine fix beside the port), M1 (a seed outside its folders). **About six arrivals of the owner's attention across fifteen links.**

## Not in this chain

- #1346 (the `taskScheduler` config move) stays behind #1317; S1 leaves the config reader where it is.
- #1816 (the pack-boundary retrospective) stays under #1317; V2 is this plan's own.
- #1328 (the `updates/*` shims) is #1317's last code link.
- Simplifying the unit-test tree itself (re-homing tests onto stage entry points) — a later plan, once R shows which module paths the tests still need.

## The retrospective's brief (V2, written now)

Expected after the chain, against the numbers M1 records before R0:

| Measure | Now | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| non-test modules in the pack | 90 | ≤ 60 |
| non-test lines | ~11,000 | ≤ 7,000 |
| design-doc lines under `docs/` | 9,483 | ≤ 400 |
| scenarios | 82 | ≥ 100; the sim suite ≤ 5 s |

Signals — misuse: a barrier finding on a stage edge, or a waiver added to let one through. Overuse: a shim still imported after S2. Underuse: a scenario cited by no principle; a panel nobody opened (page hits are not recorded — say so). {"number":1890,"title":"claudinite-tasks: roles as folders — src/<role>/, typed world ports, queue/ frozen as ABI","body":"Link **S1** of #1869. Refs #1869 #1478 — this is one link of a longer chain, so it closes neither.

`packs/claudinite-tasks/` was the old flat `engine/scheduler/` copied in whole (#1326): 32 modules at the root, a `queue/` that was both workflow ABI and most of the logic, and REST paths spread over a dozen modules. Every module now sits in the role it plays, and the graph between the roles is enforced rather than described.

## What moved where

| Folder | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `src/contract/` | what a task declares and what it means — `task-contract`, `task-declaration{,-text}`, `task-defaults`, `task-terms`, `task-trailer`, `model-map`, `precondition-policy`, `calendar`, `merge-policy`, `built-in-tasks`, `discover`, `dormancy`, and the new `precondition.mjs` (the seam extracted from the executor) |
| `src/items/` | the work item as data — `work-item`, `leases`, `anchors`, `apply-status`, `read`, `run-record`, `tracker`, `usage-format`, `pr-fields`, and `pick-order` (also extracted from the executor) |
| `src/world/` | the only outward edges — `github.mjs` (the REST client and **every** call site's operation, named), `actions.mjs`, `sessions.mjs`, `git.mjs`, `processes.mjs`, `clock.mjs` |
| `src/signals/` | `index`, `context`, `fleet`, `for-task` (was `queue/signals.mjs`) |
| `src/schedule/` | `run` (was `queue/scheduler-run`), `readiness`, `create-work-item`, `drain-dispatch` |
| `src/execute/` | `loop` (was `queue/executor`), `heartbeat`, `suspend`, `target`, `code-work`, `code-work-run`, `prework-run`, the three env bags |
| `src/session/` | `converge-item`, `verify-outcome`, `record-exec`, `resolve-dispatch`, `validate-dispatch`, `dispatch` |
| `src/deliver/` | `land-pr`, `deliver-generated`, `deliver-pr.md` |
| `src/recover/` | `janitor-rules`, `workflow-failure`, `continuation` |
| `src/adopt/` | `converge-workflows`, `hash-minute` |
| `queue/` | the six frozen entry points as runnable shims, `instructions.md`, `tasks/implement-request/` — nothing else |
| `test/` | mirrors `src/`; `test/sim/` moved only its import paths |

`packs/claudinite-tasks/*.mjs` is now `pack.mjs` alone.

## Enforcement, landed with the tree

Two declared checks in `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/declared-checks.json`, both silent on the moved tree:

- **`tasks-stage-barriers`** — `forbidReferences` beside the existing `pack-independence` edge. `contract/` and `items/` name no stage and no world; `world/` imports at most `contract` and `items`; each stage imports only `contract`, `items`, `world`, `signals` and the stages below it (`execute` → `deliver`, `session` → `deliver`); nothing under `src/` imports `queue/` or `shared-code/`. Every rule's scope is non-empty against the real tree.
- **`tasks-world-edges-live-in-world`** — a line match keeping `fetch(`, `process.env`, `node:child_process`, argless `new Date()` and `Date.now(` under `src/` inside `src/world/` only.

## Deviations from the brief, and why

- **`pick-order.mjs` sits in `src/items/`, not `src/schedule/`.** Both stages ask it — the executor to choose what to claim, the scheduler run for `pickableCount`'s drain gate — and `items/` is the only role both may import. Putting it in `schedule/` would have created the execute → schedule edge the extraction exists to remove.
- **`continuation.mjs` sits in `src/recover/`, not `src/execute/`.** It escalates on `workflow-failure`'s surface, so placing it in `execute/` would have created an execute → recover edge. It is recovery by what it does.
- **`new Date()` is read as the argless clock read.** #1869's *End state* writes `new Date()`; the S1 text writes `new Date(`. Forbidding the latter would have moved `calendar.mjs` and every ISO-string parse into `world/`, which is arithmetic rather than an outward edge. The check forbids the clock read and leaves parsing where it is used; the module header says so.
- **The GitHub port is a module of named operations over the injected `gh`, not yet a bound port object.** Every REST path the pack calls is spelled in `src/world/github.mjs` and nowhere else, which is what makes the edge countable. Converting the *seam* from `gh(path)` to a port object means rewriting every test's fake, which is H1's job (`test/sim/world/`) and would have changed tests here, against this link's own shape.

## What this link leaves behind

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/docs/PRINCIPLES.md` — the mechanism as claims, and the only file under `docs/`.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/coverage.test.mjs` rewritten as the two-way claim guard.

- A pull request for the owner's review (no automerge: the principles are the design).

## What counts as this link having worked

Read back on `main` after merge: `ls packs/claudinite-tasks/docs` prints `PRINCIPLES.md` alone; the whole suite is green (`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`); `grep -rn "DESIGN §\|SCENARIOS.md\|RESEARCH.md\|§[0-9]" packs --include=*.mjs --include=*.md --include=*.json` hits nothing outside `PRINCIPLES.md`; the guard has a test in each direction.

## The playbook

**Write the principles from the sources, before reading any narrative.** Sources, in this order: the coverage map in `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/README.md` (each row is a claim and its scenarios), the scenario titles in `test/sim/scenarios.test.mjs`, then the mechanism sections of `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` (§3–§12, §16, §17), `docs/task-preconditions/DESIGN.md` and `docs/task-code-work/DESIGN.md`, then §15's decisions (each survives only as the claim it decided, with its rejected alternative on one line).

**The claim form.** One bullet per claim, present tense, *the outcome when the condition holds* — `A no-go at pick closes the item; the next occurrence is the next tick's ask.` — never an actor narrative (`the executor should close…`). Each claim ends with the tests that prove it in backticks: a scenario's first word (`S13'`, `S59`) or, for what the simulator cannot see (a label spelling, a record format), `<test file>: <test title>` from the unit suite. One optional line beneath a claim for *why*, one for *rejected: … because …*. No dates, no names, no history, no "as of", no superseded sections. Group the claims by the roles #1869 names (schedule, execute, session, deliver, recover, requests, cost, contract).

**A claim with no test.** Either write the scenario now (in the current simulator, keeping `sim.mjs`'s model in step — the scenario title is the durable identifier the later harness keeps) or leave the claim out. The document may end with a short *Not yet verifiable* list, each entry naming what it would take; that list is not a claim.

**The guard.** Rewrite `coverage.test.mjs` to read `PRINCIPLES.md` instead of DESIGN §15: every cited scenario word matches a test title's first word in `scenarios.test.mjs` and every cited unit test exists; and every test in `scenarios.test.mjs` is cited by at least one claim. Watch it fail once each way (a made-up citation; an uncited scenario) before the real run.

**Delete, section by section.** For each section of the seven documents (`tasks-dispatch/{DESIGN,SCENARIOS,RESEARCH}.md`, `task-preconditions/DESIGN.md`, `task-code-work/{DESIGN.md,check-fix-subsumption-audit.md}`, `per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md`): confirm it is carried by a principle, a module header, or the pack README; a still-true description with no home goes into the header of the module it describes, as current state, never as history. Then delete the file. The `test/sim/README.md` keeps how to run and the working discipline (now: *write the scenario first, then the code*); its coverage map and "unsimulated world" table move into `PRINCIPLES.md` (the second as the *Not yet verifiable* list).

**Sweep the pointers** (load `repo-text-sweeps` first). 54 pack modules, 29 test files and other packs' prose cite `DESIGN §n`, `SCENARIOS`, `RESEARCH`. Re-point each at `PRINCIPLES.md#<anchor>` where the sentence still needs the reference; drop the citation where the sentence only cited itself. Do not reword the comments otherwise.

**Vocabulary.** No new term. Role names are #1869's. If a claim needs a word the code does not already use, file a question issue and write the claim without it.

**If anything above cannot be done** (a claim you cannot source, a test you cannot make green): comment here what was read and what is missing, leave this issue open, and converge as `action`.

The saga is [#1869 — Reorganize claudinite-tasks: roles as folders, the simulator as the harness, principles as the spec](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1869) (plan approved 2026-09-07, 15 links). **It has been stalled at link 2 of 15 for six days, on your review, and the stalled PR has now gone conflicted.**

### Where the chain stands

| Link | Issue | State |
|---|---|---|
| **P** — principles as the spec | [#1870](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1870) | ✅ merged — `packs/claudinite-tasks/docs/PRINCIPLES.md` is the only file under `docs/` |
| **S1** — the re-shelve into `src/<role>/` | [#1478](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1478) | 🟡 delivered as [PR #1890](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1890), parked `needs-human-approval` since 2026-09-07. Policy is `nothing`, so only you can land it |
| H1, H2 | [#1347](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1347), [#1871](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1871) | ⛔ `blocked` behind S1 |
| M1, M2 | [#1872](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1872), [#1874](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1874) | ⛔ `blocked` behind S1 |
| V1 | [#1873](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1873) | ⛔ `blocked` behind S1 |
| R0–R5 (the rewrites) | [#1875](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1875), [#1876](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1876), [#1877](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1877), [#1878](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1878), [#1879](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1879), [#1880](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1880) | ⛔ `blocked`, chained behind H2 |
| V2 — retrospective | [#1881](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1881) | ⛔ `blocked` |

So the *rebuild* half (R0–R5) has not started at all — nothing has been simplified yet. `main` still carries the flat pack: `ls packs/claudinite-tasks/*.mjs` shows the 30-odd root modules.

### What #1890 actually contains

214 files, +3307/−2732: every module moved into `src/{contract,items,world,signals,schedule,execute,session,deliver,recover,adopt}/`, the six `queue/*.mjs` reduced to runnable ABI shims, `shared-code/` unchanged from outside, plus two new declared checks (`tasks-stage-barriers`, `tasks-world-edges-live-in-world`). Its own exit read: 3393 pass / 1 fail, the failure being the shallow-clone guard that fails identically on `main`. The second comment on #1869 is a self-correction worth knowing — the first "checks green" read was an artifact of grepping `^[BLOCKING]` while both new checks sat in their fortnight advisory window; seven real violations were found and the tree moved to satisfy the rules.

### The new problem

`main` has moved 15 commits since, five of them inside `packs/claudinite-tasks`. A test-merge of the branch against `origin/main` now reports **6 conflicts** — `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `src/signals/index.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-dashboard/test/pack.test.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/test/task-policies.test.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/RULES.md`, plus a file-location conflict for `test/queue/wake-own-writes.test.mjs` (added on `main` inside a directory the branch renamed). Every further day of `main` commits touching that pack widens this, because S1 moves the whole tree.

Separately, [#1816 "Retrospective: the claudinite-tasks pack boundary"](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1816) is parked `needs-human-decision` (touched yesterday) — the plan puts it outside this chain, under [#1317](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1317).

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own — research it against the vendor's live documentation, capture what is portable as a technology skill with declared checks, and wire the project's use of it as a task in its structural local pack. Use when asked to make a repo do something with a technology nobody there has used yet (host it on X, send through Y, publish to Z), or to "research how to do this correctly" and "create a skill" for it.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- running-the-suite: Running this repo's test suite — the one command that covers it, reading a run's output from a file instead of re-running it, iterating on the tests an edit touches, and staging a new test file before certifying a run. Use before any node --test.
- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- working-with-generated-files: Working with a file a test or tool generates — naming it, changing the generator rather than the file, and resolving its merge conflicts by regenerating. Loaded for any edit of a GENERATED file.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, get the owner's approval of the plan itself — a line per step, the dependency graph, each link's automerge policy — before filing any of its issues, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, size the links (how many PRs, what each one's diff is predicted to touch and the automerge policy that prediction becomes) and write the chain to survive a policy park, a red CI or a PR closed unmerged, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — when asked to run a plan as a chain of ad-hoc tasks, and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written — RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon — brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, and the per-pack references doc. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, and when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-repo-scanning-checks: How a check that scans the repo picks its file set, strips comments before matching a forbidden token, and proves itself silent against real sources. Loaded for any edit of a coded or declared check.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.json or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. entries.description: List issues in a GitHub repository. For pagination, use the 'endCursor' from the previous response's 'pageInfo' in the 'after' parameter.

after.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the cursor from the previous response.

direction.description: Order direction. If provided, the 'orderBy' also needs to be provided.

field_name.description: Name of the custom field (e.g. "Priority"). Case-insensitive.

value.description: Value to filter on. For single-select fields, the option name (e.g. "P1"). For dates, YYYY-MM-DD. For numbers, the numeric value as a string. For text, the text value.

field_filters.description: Filter by custom issue field values. Each entry takes a field_name and a value; the server looks up the field and coerces the value to its type (single-select option name, text, number, or YYYY-MM-DD date).

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each issue. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' and 'field_values' in particular drops the largest per-result data.

orderBy.description: Order issues by field. If provided, the 'direction' also needs to be provided.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

state.description: Filter by state, by default both open and closed issues are returned when not provided

{"number":1347,"title":"Merge the dispatch simulator into the scheduler codebase — the sim becomes a test harness","body":"Blocked-by: #1478
Model: opus
Automerge: under:packs/claudinite-tasks/test

Link **H1** of #1869. The analysis below is the original (2026-08-24); the **Brief** at the end is what binds this run where the two differ.

---

`packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/sim.mjs` (1310 lines) imports **nothing** from the engine: it is a second implementation of the dispatch mechanism beside `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/`. Now that the design is shipped (§17's cadence included), the model no longer runs ahead of the code, so the duplication buys nothing and can drift silently. Fold it: keep the harness, delete the model, and drive the **real** modules from it.

## The drift surface

| sim.mjs | engine |
|---|---|
| `mostRecentAnchor` / `nextAnchor` / `periodMs` / `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` | `queue/anchors.mjs`, `calendar.mjs` (its own comment says "mirroring") |
| `statusOf` + the legacy-label decode | `queue/work-item.mjs` |
| `writeBoardRow` / `boardRow` | `queue/schedule-board.mjs` |
| `schedulerRun()` — four jobs, both occurrence guards, adoption, reclaim | `planSchedulerRun` + the shell in `queue/scheduler-run.mjs` |
| `pickable()`, `claim()`, `postClaimVerify()` | `pickOrder`, `claimWinner`, `conflictsWithEarlierClaim` |
| `janitor()` | `queue/janitor-rules.mjs` |
| `eligible` / `gatedModel` / `APPROVAL_RE` | `built-in-tasks.mjs`'s `APPROVAL_RE`, `parseRequestFields` |

## Why it is feasible

- Every GitHub call in `queue/` goes through one function — `gh(path, { method, body })` from `signals/gh.mjs` — over 19 distinct paths (issues, labels, comments, permission, Actions variables, workflow dispatch).
- A fake GitHub at exactly that seam already exists in `test/queue/executor-loop.test.mjs` (~45 lines) and already drives the real `runExecutor` end to end.
- `runExecutor` is already fully injectable: `now`, `random`, `heldNow`, `collectSignalsFor`, `runTaskCodeWork`, `invokeAgent`, `log`.
- The pure cores are already exported: `planSchedulerRun`, `pickOrder`, `claimWinner`, `noGoPlan`, `evaluatePrecondition`, the janitor rules.

The enabling gap: `scheduler-run.mjs`'s shell (`main`, exported as `runSchedulerRun`) is argless — it reads `process.cwd()`, `process.env`, `new Date()`, `makeGh()`. Same for the janitor and drain-dispatch shells. They need `runExecutor`'s parameter shape, with `main()` as the argless wrapper.

## What survives — the harness proper

- the virtual clock and ordered event queue (`seq` modelling comment-id order);
- the platform behaviours: the cron grid / `cronHours`, dropped and late fires, stale snapshots for `raceExecutorsAt`, `eventLost`, the absent/corrupt board, `gone`/`unreadable` issues, the collaborator permission table;
- `actionExecutions()`, which gets stronger: the fake counts the engine's real `workflow_dispatch` calls instead of the model's own runs;
- the scenario DSL — 12 methods across 1994 lines of `scenarios.test.mjs`, whose assertions mostly read the issue store the fake GitHub also has, so most scenarios should port largely intact;
- the README's coverage map and "The unsimulated world" table — the second one becomes literally "what the fake `gh` does not do".

## The cost, accepted deliberately

Two independent expressions of the design can disagree, and the disagreement is a signal; afterwards the scenarios are regression tests against captured behaviour, not a cross-check of implementation against spec. That independence is already given up by the standing rule (*"model what the engine's code actually writes, never the rule's stated intent"*), and the design is shipped, so the oracle role has lapsed. Consequence to land in the same change: the sim README's "change the simulator first" becomes "write the engine's pure core first, drive it from the harness".

## Phasing (one PR per slice)

1. Promote the fake GitHub out of `executor-loop.test.mjs` into a shared world (issue store, comment ids, labels, permission API, Actions variables, dispatch capture), plus the clock and event queue. No behaviour change — the existing loop test proves the fake still works.
2. Give the scheduler-run, janitor and drain shells `runExecutor`'s injectable shape; `main()` becomes the argless wrapper.
3. Port scenarios in slices, deleting the matching sim model as each goes green: anchors, then the board, pick/claim, janitor, requests, the executions accounting last.
4. `sim.mjs` ends as world + DSL only; `coverage.test.mjs` and the README tables carry over.

Each slice is red-first by construction: it fails where the engine and the model disagreed, and that failure is the finding.

---

## Brief (link H1 of #1869, 2026-09-07)

Read #1869's *End state* and *Standing conditions* first. This link is phase 1 of the list above; phase 2 landed with S1 (#1478); phases 3–4 are H2 (#1871). The seam is no longer `gh(path)`: S1 made `src/world/` a set of **typed ports**, and the fake implements the same names.

**Ready when:** #1478 has merged — `packs/claudinite-tasks/src/world/github.mjs` exists on `main` and exports named operations. Absent: comment, leave open, converge as `action` naming #1478.

**Build `packs/claudinite-tasks/test/sim/world/`**, one module per port, each exporting a factory returning an object with exactly the real port's method names:
- `clock.mjs` — virtual time and the ordered event queue (from today's `sim.mjs`; strictly time-ordered, FIFO within a tie, no wall clock);
- `github.mjs` — the in-memory repo: issues with labels, bodies, state, timestamps; comments with server-assigned strictly increasing ids and 1-second timestamps; label definitions (422 on applying an unknown one); pull requests; refs and contents as needed by `deliver/`; the collaborator permission table; Actions variables; `workflow_dispatch` captured as an event for `actions.mjs`. Faults, each off by default and switchable per scenario: rate-limit `403` for N calls, a stale list (creation not yet visible), a torn label swap (remove lands, add fails), a dropped `labeled` event. Promote the fake repo from `test/queue/executor-loop.test.mjs` as the starting point;
- `actions.mjs` — workflow runs as first-class events: the cron grid with late and dropped fires, start latency, the scheduler's concurrency group, a dispatched executor run, job death at a timeout, `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, the hold variable read through the GitHub port; a ledger of runs with start and end instants (the successor of `actionExecutions()`, and the billed-minutes source);
- `sessions.mjs` — the routine fire with the fired / refused / unanswered trichotomy, and the fired session as a scheduled event that runs `agents.mjs`;
- `agents.mjs` — scripted agentic work: a session runs the real session-side code (`src/session/`, `src/deliver/`) against the fake GitHub and does what its script says — leaves a PR or none, prints its record, takes N virtual minutes with heartbeats, dies, refuses;
- `humans.mjs` — a person's actions as events: mark an issue, edit a label, approve or merge a PR, close, comment.

**Parity guard:** a test asserting each fake exports every method of its real port and nothing else, so a new operation on the real side fails here before a scenario silently bypasses it.

**Move `executor-loop.test.mjs` onto the shared fake** with its assertions unchanged — that is the proof the fake still works. Touch no scenario and no model in `sim.mjs`; that is H2's.

**Vocabulary:** none new. Module names are #1869's.

**Exit, read back on `main`:** the six modules exist under `test/sim/world/`, the parity test is green, `executor-loop.test.mjs` imports the shared fake, the whole suite is green.

**How it ends:** one PR under the policy above (`Refs #1869 #1347`, never `Closes #1869`); an edit outside `test/` parks it, which is intended. Comment the exit reads on #1869; converge through `converge-item.mjs`. Closing this issue releases H2 (#1871).

{"number":1478,"title":"Re-shelve claudinite-tasks by stage: src/ for the code, queue/ frozen as workflow ABI","body":"Blocked-by: #1870
Model: opus

Link **S1** of #1869. The analysis below is the original (2026-08-30); the 2026-09-07 comment validates each claim against `main`, and the **Brief** at the end is what binds this run where the two differ.

---

`packs/claudinite-tasks/` carries ~24 modules at its root. That is sediment, not design: `git log --follow` on any of them shows one event — `a248483` (#1326) copied the whole flat `engine/scheduler/` directory in with `C100`. The pack root *is* the old flat scheduler dir, and `queue/` is the one sub-system that had already been carved out inside it before the move.

## The stages are already separable

An import graph over the pack (tests excluded) collapses to five stages with **exactly one** backward edge:

| Stage | Cross-stage edges |
|---|---|
| schedule — `scheduler-run`, `readiness`, `schedule-board`, `create-work-item`, `tick`, `drain-dispatch` | ⚠️ one: `queue/scheduler-run.mjs:32` imports `pickOrder` from `queue/executor.mjs` |
| execute-code — `code-work`, `code-work-run`, `prework-run`, `secrets-bag` | none |
| execute-agent — `resolve-dispatch`, `validate-dispatch`, `invoke`, `executor-continuation` | none |
| finalize — `converge-item`, `verify-outcome`, `record-exec`, `land-pr`, `deliver-generated` | none (invoked as CLI from prose, never imported by the executor) |
| recover — `janitor-rules`, `workflow-failure`, `task-janitor` | none |

That edge is placement, not coupling. `queue/executor.mjs` (672 lines) hosts two functions that are not executor mechanics: `pickOrder` (ordering policy over the queue, called by the scheduler run) and `evaluatePrecondition` (the contract's evaluator, published through `shared-code/task-contract.mjs` and re-run by both sides). Extract those two and the DAG is strictly one-directional — at which point the `barriers` pack can enforce it pointed inward, with no bespoke check.

The kernel is small and falls out of fan-in: `queue/work-item.mjs` (14 importers), `merge-policy.mjs` (6), `calendar.mjs` / `task-contract.mjs` / `queue/anchors.mjs` (5 each), `run-record.mjs` (4), `queue/leases.mjs` (3).

## What cannot move

Two of these cannot be repaired by a converge, and they shape the whole layout:

1. **Workflow `run:` targets** — stamped into every member's `.github/workflows/` at adoption, the one directory a converge may never push to. Five frozen paths: `queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `queue/drain-dispatch.mjs`, `queue/workflow-failure.mjs`, `queue/executor.mjs`, `queue/executor-continuation.mjs`. Moving one costs a human-merged PR per member.
2. **`executor.md` and `queue/instructions.md`** — CCR routine endpoints, a per-repo console setting (`adopt-pack` §4b). Moving one needs every member re-pointed by hand.
3. Engine-mandated names: `pack.mjs`, `worldRules/`, `workRules/`, `tasks/`, `skills/`, `migrations/` and the metadata files.

So `queue/` survives as exactly **five one-line re-export shims plus `instructions.md`**, with a header saying it is workflow ABI and may never hold logic again. Everything else internal goes under `src/`.

## `shared-code/` → `src/contract/`, with shims

The barrier's allow list names `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code` as the one path another pack may import (`.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/declared-checks.json`). The nine modules there are all `export *` — 52 lines total — so they curate nothing today; their whole value is being a stable address. `contract` names that better, and absorbs the existing `task-contract` sense rather than colliding with it: what a task must declare, and what another pack may import.

**It needs shims.** `planPackUpdates` (`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs:76`) marks a pack `blocked` when its `minEngineVersion` exceeds the member's engine — **that pack alone is held back while its siblings land**. So a member can hold a new `claudinite-dashboard` beside a blocked `claudinite-tasks`; if the dashboard imports `src/contract/…` and the mount carries only `shared-code/`, that pack fails to load, the mount fails its self-test, the converge refuses to land at all, and the member cannot receive the version that would fix it. That is the #1004 class exactly. So: move the modules, leave `shared-code/*` re-exporting, retire them on a stamp-confirmable precondition — "no member's `packVersions['claudinite-tasks']` predates the rename" — never a date.

Reference inventory: 15 non-test import sites across 5 consumer packs (dashboard ×5, fleet-sheepdog, basics, growth, lifecycle), 17 in tests, 13 prose/config mentions, the barrier's allow-list string (which must name both paths during the window), and one cross-pack path reference in `claudinite-dashboard/test/pack.test.mjs` reading `claudinite-tasks/stubs/…`.

## Target layout

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/
  pack.mjs  README.md  VERSIONS.md  badge.svg
  executor.md                          ← frozen (console routine)
  worldRules/  workRules/  tasks/  migrations/     ← engine-mandated

  queue/                               ← FROZEN WORKFLOW ABI, nothing else ever
    scheduler-run.mjs  drain-dispatch.mjs  workflow-failure.mjs
    executor.mjs  executor-continuation.mjs        (5 one-line re-exports)
    instructions.md                    ← frozen (console routine)

  src/
    contract/    work-items  anchors  task-contract  merge-policy  signals
                 github  delivery  usage-format  wake          (barrier-allowed)
    model/       work-item  leases  calendar  anchors  task-contract
                 precondition ←extracted  merge-policy  model-map  run-record
                 built-in-tasks  discover  dispatch
    gh/          read  write  tracker  read-items
    signals/     collectors + for-task
    schedule/    run  readiness  schedule-board  create-work-item  tick
                 drain-dispatch  pick-order ←extracted
    execute/     loop  apply-status  heartbeat  suspend
      code/      code-work  run  prework-run  secrets-bag
      agent/     resolve-dispatch  validate-dispatch  invoke  continuation
      built-in/implement-request/   (NOT tasks/ — engine-owned, registered separately)
    finalize/    converge-item  verify-outcome  record-exec  land-pr
                 deliver-generated  narrow-diff  deliver-pr.md
    recover/     janitor-rules  workflow-failure
    adopt/       converge-workflows  hash-minute  stubs/

  shared-code/   ← 9 re-export shims → src/contract/, retired on the stamp
  test/          mirrors src/
```

231	
232	// Rule G — THE ENDED PARK (#1468). A park states what a person owes; nothing watched
233	// for that debt being PAID. An approval park in particular holds an open pull
234	// request, which is why rule E excludes it — a later clean run does not answer it —
235	// so once the pull request merged the item sat open until somebody read it.
236	//
237	// `Ends-when: #<n> closed` is the item's own answer to "what would end this", and
238	// the resolution of that target is the verdict:
239	//
240	//   merged   → the work this park was holding LANDED, so the item is `done`
241	//   closed   → the task was REJECTED, so the item is `rejected`
242	//
243	// The distinction is the whole point of reading merged-ness rather than state: a
244	// park closed as `rejected` when its pull request in fact merged would report a
245	// delivered run as one that never happened.
246	//
247	// EITHER OUTCOME ENDS THE ITEM, and the shell closes the issue on both. A person
248	// who closed the pull request unmerged has already said what happens to this run;
249	// an item left open under that verdict is the queue asking them to say it twice.
250	//
251	// `resolutionOf(n)` answers `'merged' | 'closed' | null` — null for open, unknown,
252	// or unreadable, all of which mean the park stands. Only parked items: a live item
253	// is the machinery working, and an item still with an agent has not ended anything.
254	export function endedParkItems(open = [], { resolutionOf = () => null } = {}) {
255	  return open.filter((item) => {
256	    if (!isParked(item)) return false;
257	    const { endsWhen } = parseWorkItemBody(item.body);
258	    if (endsWhen == null) return false;
259	    return resolutionOf(endsWhen) != null;
260	  });
261	}
262	
263	export const endedParkComment = (target, resolution) => (resolution === 'merged'
264	  ? `#${target} merged, which is what this item was parked waiting for. Closing it \`${STATUS_DONE}\` — `
265	    + 'the work landed and there is nothing left for anyone to do here.'
266	  : `#${target} was closed without merging, which ends what this item was parked waiting for. `
267	    + `Closing it \`${STATUS_REJECTED}\` — nothing landed, so if the work is still wanted, re-queue it (${requeueHint}).`);
268	
269	// The period of a task, for rule A — read from the cadence term its declaration
270	// at HEAD states; null (a day, in rule A) for a task that keeps none.
271	export const periodForTasks = (tasks = []) => {
272	  const byId = new Map(tasks.map((t) => [`${t.pack}/${t.id}`, t]));
273	  return (id) => taskPeriodMs(byId.get(id)?.decl);
274	};
275	
276	// Rule H — THE UNCLOSED TERMINAL (#1526). A terminal status says the item is over:
277	// `done` means nothing is left for anyone to act on, `rejected` that nothing will
278	// happen. Every writer closes the issue in the same breath — so an open one wearing
279	// one is a transition that TORE, or a session that improvised its converge by hand
280	// and stopped at the label (#1220, #1265). Either way the item then reads as
281	// finished to every rule here and to the leash, while sitting open in the queue's
282	// count forever: the one state nothing else recovers.
283	//
284	// The close is the whole of the repair, and the outcome is the status's own — a
285	// `done` item closes `completed`, a `rejected` one `not_planned`. Nothing is
286	// relabelled: the status was already right, it was the close that never happened.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
